editorial:
Imagine getting totally tricked into thinking a fancy manor house is actually a cheap hotel. That is exactly what happens to Charles Marlow and George Hastings in this funny story. You will love how the plot kicks off when Tony, the mischievous brother, plays a huge prank on the visitors. The vibe is light and breezy, focusing on the awkward social gaps between rich and poor. You get to watch Kate, a smart young woman, navigate her father's strict rules while dealing with a suitor who acts like a totally different person depending on who he thinks he is talking to.

The acting is great because the cast really nails the silly misunderstandings and fast talking. While the pacing starts a bit slow, the comedy picks up once everyone is under one roof. If you enjoy witty banter and romantic mix-ups, you should definitely give this a go.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when Marlow realizes he has been tricked into thinking the Hardcastle home was an inn. After all the lies and fake identities, Kate reveals her true status as the daughter of the house. Marlow admits he actually loves her, even though he was rude at first. The couple gets engaged, and the other side plots are settled, leaving everyone happy and the prankster Tony satisfied with the chaos he caused.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves romantic comedies and funny misunderstandings.
